newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures finish mixed, S&P lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures finish mixed, S&P lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mixed after an afternoon of choppy trading.
Profit-taking plagued most contracts early and September Standard and Poor's 500 futures fell though key 900.00, but September recovered near midday to post a fresh record high at 908.50.
The contract cut its gains into the close but managed to stay above key 900.00, traders noted.
Overall, traders said they were pleased that S&Ps so decisively rejected their early session low considering weak bonds and ongoing worries of profit-taking.
Early in the session, stronger than expected May industrial production and capacity use data pushed September Treasury bonds to session lows. September S&P 500s fell in sympathy.
At 0815 CDT/1315 GMT, May industrial output was reported up 0.4 percent and April's production was revised to up 0.3 percent. Capacity use gained to 83.7 from 83.6 in April.
But while T-bonds remained lethargic all day, stock index futures were able to recover from their lows, traders said.
"It was pretty strong the way they came back," a trader said. "They came back with a whole head of steam there."
Traders said June/September spread activity was active most of the session as Thursday's expiration of June contracts nears. One trader estimated spread volume at 20,000.

Traders said mild resistance was clustered now around the latest record highs at 906.40 from Monday, 907.15 this morning and 908.50. But they noted that September S&Ps have been very resilient and have needed only very mild sell-offs to wipe out overbought conditions.
Support was seen at 900.00 and at 902.50.

Before the open, the consumer price index (CPI) was reported up 0.1 percent overall in May and gained 0.2 percent excluding volatile food and energy components. CPI had been forecast up 0.2 percent in both the overall and core rates.

At the close, September S&Ps were down 1.40 points to 902.75, Value Lines rose 2.35 to 795.00, Nikkei lost 215.00 to 20,650.0, Midcap gained 1.45 to 293.00, NYSE Composite lost 0.95 to 469.25, Russell rose 0.45 to 398.75, and Nasdaq gained 9.90 to 1000.40.
